sources.title: zk-ScalHard: Scalable and Hardware-Rooted Privacy-Preserving Authentication for Secure OTA Updates in Zonal SDVs
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: zk-ScalHard proposes hierarchical decentralized OTA authentication for zonal SDVs using silicon PUFs plus ZKP circuits for zonal identity/integrity and HPC aggregation.
The authors claim O(1) communication and verification complexity versus linear O(n) scaling for the compared PKI/Uptane-oriented baseline.
The v2 abstract reports 99.2% lower authentication bandwidth and 99.9% lower temporal attack surface in its evaluation.

metrics.name: reported authentication-bandwidth reduction
metrics.context: Author-reported comparison against Uptane in the v2 abstract.

metrics.name: motivating OTA ECU scale
metrics.context: Architecture scale stated in the abstract motivation.

limitations.text: The accessible primary abstract does not expose cryptographic security assumptions, benchmark ECU/zonal topology, proof sizes, prover/verifier hardware, latency/energy costs, Uptane configuration, or exact definition of temporal attack surface.
Claims of 100% data sovereignty, GDPR compliance and the very large percentage reductions are author claims and require full methodology/security-model inspection before editorial use.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for zk-ScalHard: Scalable and Hardware-Rooted Privacy-Preserving Authentication for Secure OTA Updates in Zonal SDVs; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The v2 primary abstract verifies the PUF/ZKP hierarchical design and reports O(1), 99.2% and 99.9% claims, but benchmark/security-model details are unresolved.

unresolved_questions: Inspect the full v2 report/repository for threat model, ZKP circuits, proof/prover/verifier costs, topology scale, Uptane baseline and definitions behind the 99.2%/99.9% results.

editorial.why_now_note: Zonal OTA shifts trust aggregation toward zone controllers/HPCs, making credential/privacy scaling an architecture-level concern rather than only a backend-security detail.
editorial.rationale: Security architecture is highly relevant, but the unusually strong scalability/privacy/compliance claims require full verification before they can support the report.
